title: COMPOS (Comprehensive Oxford Maths and Physics Online School)
text: Scheme run by Oxford Uni for state-school pupils in years 10-13 involving uni-level maths and physics problems. Every week you receive a 90 minute tutorial from a current student as well as an online lecture about the assignment, running over the school year. They especially encourage students from groups underrepresented in STEM to apply!
demographics: Must be studying maths and physics A Level if applying to the year 12 or 13 scheme
Updated text: Join COMPOS, a program from Oxford University that offers state-school students in grades 10-13 the chance to tackle university-level math and physics problems. Each week, you'll receive a 90-minute tutorial from a current Oxford student and an online lecture on the assignment. This year-long program is especially keen on encouraging students from underrepresented groups in STEM to apply.

title: HCGEC Essay Competition
text: HCGEC Essay Competition provides a platform for young, ambitious high school students to exercise their writing skills and compete with students from all over the world! There are three writing categories: creative, argumentative,  and journalistic. Prompts are released shortly after the competition starts. Registrations open in November.
Updated text: Calling all aspiring writers! The HCGEC Essay Competition invites high school students worldwide to showcase their writing prowess. Choose from three categories: creative, argumentative, or journalistic. Unleash your imagination, craft compelling arguments, or report on current events. Prompts will be revealed soon after the competition launch. Don't miss out on this opportunity to connect with fellow writers and showcase your literary talents!

title: SARC Research Competition
text: The High School Academic Research Competition is where talented students from around the world compete to present high-quality research on any topic. SARC challenges students to sharpen their critical thinking skills, immerse themselves in the research process, and hone their writing skills for success.
Updated text: Calling all curious minds! Join the SARC Research Competition, where you'll dive into the world of research and showcase your intellectual prowess. Explore any topic that sparks your passion, from science to history to the arts. Sharpen your critical thinking, immerse yourself in the research process, and develop exceptional writing skills. This competition is your chance to shine as a young researcher and make your mark on the academic landscape.

title: ISRO Young Scientist Programme
text: The course will impart basic knowledge on Space Technology, Space Science and Space Applications to the younger students in emerging trends in space science and technology amongst the youngsters, who are the future building blocks of our nation. ISRO has chalked out this programme to "Catch them young".
Updated text: Calling all future space explorers! ISRO's Young Scientist Programme is your chance to dive into the fascinating world of space. This program will ignite your passion for space science, technology, and applications. By joining, you'll gain a solid foundation in these fields, setting you on a path to contribute to India's future in space exploration and innovation.

title: Ashoka University Young Scholars Programme
text: Ashoka’s Young Scholars Programmes (YSP) are certified, summer, residential programmes, designed to give motivated students in classes 9,10,11 & 12 an exposure to a liberal arts & sciences education at the university  level. We are offering five inter- & transdisciplinary programme options during the summer break. YSP 2024 offers five interdisciplinary streams with a hands-on approach to learning. YSP 2024, for the very first time, is being offered in two sessions, May 20 – May 31, 2024 OR June 3 – June 14, 2024
location: Ashoka University, Electronic City, Bengaluru, Karnataka
duration: Normal courses: 5 days, Advanced courses: 10 days
Updated text: Immerse yourself in a university-level learning experience this summer with Ashoka University's Young Scholars Programme! Designed for high schoolers in grades 9-12, this residential program offers five interdisciplinary streams that combine hands-on learning with a liberal arts and sciences approach. Choose from topics like global challenges, data science, and creative writing, and engage in thought-provoking discussions, hands-on experiments, and collaborative projects. With two sessions available in May and June, you can tailor your experience to your schedule and explore the world of higher education while making lasting connections with fellow scholars.

title: Youth Citizen Entrepreneurship Competition
text: The Citizen Entrepreneurship Competition (CEC) aims to empower entrepreneurs – especially young ones – to work for a more peaceful and sustainable world. Participants are invited to submit their ideas and projects with social impact and to make a concrete commitment to one or more of the 17 UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and to implement them. The 17 goals for sustainable development address the most important social, economic, environmental and health challenges of our time. The submissions are divided into two categories: idea and project. Entrepreneurs from 13 years old are invited to submit their idea or project to participate in the CEC.
Updated text: Calling all young innovators! Join the Youth Citizen Entrepreneurship Competition and make a difference in the world. Submit your ideas or projects that tackle social issues and align with the UN's Sustainable Development Goals. Whether you're a budding entrepreneur or just have a great idea, this competition empowers you to create a positive impact on society and work towards a more sustainable future.

title: Global Genius Music Competition
text: The Global Genius Music Competition is an online classical music competition for all countries in the world. Hence there is no need to travel. We accept all classical musical instruments, singing and traditional musical instruments from the artist’s country. finds the right categories for you and our fair rating system will lead you to STARS!
Updated text: Calling all musical prodigies! The Global Genius Music Competition invites you to showcase your classical talents from the comfort of your home. title: Foyle Young Poets Award
text: The Foyle Young Poets of the Year Award is an opportunity for any young person aged 11-17 to accelerate their writing career. Since it was founded in 1998, the Award has kick-started the career of some of today’s most exciting new voices, such as Sarah Howe, Jay Bernard, Helen Mort, Richard Osmond, Caroline Bird, Phoebe Stuckes and many more poets from across the world. With entries from over 6,800 young people last year from across the UK and worldwide, it is the largest competition of its kind and its importance is widely attested.
Updated text: Calling all young poets! The Foyle Young Poets Award is your chance to ignite your writing journey. Open to ages 11-17, this prestigious award has launched the careers of renowned poets like Sarah Howe and Jay Bernard. With thousands of entries from around the globe, it's the largest competition of its kind. Join the ranks of these exceptional young voices and showcase your poetic talent on a global stage.

title: BETA Camp
text: In this 6-week program, high school students aged 13-18 can learn from experts at world-class companies like Google, IKEA, Airbnb, and more. Participants create a real-world company, reach out to influencers, and partner with them to promote a real solution. Participants also practice their skills on real companies with feedback from their top executives. Finally, all learnings go toward building your own startup with weekly guidance.
Updated text: Calling all high schoolers! Join BETA Camp, a 6-week adventure where you'll team up with experts from tech giants like Google and Airbnb. Together, you'll create a real-world company, connect with influencers, and solve real-world problems. Get hands-on experience with feedback from top executives, and build your own startup with weekly guidance. BETA Camp is your chance to turn your entrepreneurial dreams into reality!

title: Provost’s Summer Mentorship Program
text: Though this college preparatory experience is only available to Philadelphia, PA high school students, its academic rigor, excellent facilities, and no-cost status earned it a spot on our top biology opportunities for high school students list. SMP is a 4-week immersion summer program that pairs participants with one of the five affiliate University of Pennsylvania Professional Schools. It is highly competitive and typically accepts between 40-50 high school students each year.
Updated text: Calling all Philadelphia high schoolers! Join the Provost's Summer Mentorship Program, a free, four-week immersion into the world of science at the University of Pennsylvania. Get paired with a mentor from one of five professional schools and dive into cutting-edge research. With its competitive nature and limited spots, this program is a must-have for students passionate about biology and eager to explore their future in science.

title: Engineering Academy
text: This program allows high school students to experience Oxford-style teaching with practical challenges and debates. Small class sizes help students explore the concepts of hydraulics, pneumatics and the math behind engineering. The curriculum also helps students develop skills in public speaking, critical thinking and teamwork. If you’ve always wanted to immerse yourself in Oxford life, love engineering, and can afford its price tag, Engineering Academy is an amazing teen study program to pursue.
Updated text: Immerse yourself in the world of engineering at the Engineering Academy! If you're passionate about engineering and eager to experience the vibrant academic atmosphere of Oxford, this program is the perfect opportunity to ignite your curiosity and prepare for a future in the field.

title: Parsons Summer Intensive Studies
text: Parsons School of Design is a highly esteemed art school and this three-week summer program can provide a life-changing experience for arts-minded high school students. Offered in two cultural centers of the art world, this program enables students to focus on their own projects, present their work, explore the city during art and design field trips, network with guest speakers, and earn up to 3 college credits.
Updated text: Immerse yourself in the vibrant art world at Parsons School of Design's Summer Intensive Studies. title: Klossy coding program
text: Kode With Klossy camps are a series of FREE 2-week coding-intensive camps designed for students of traditionally underrepresented genders in the STEM fields. title: NYC ghetto filmmaking course

title: EnergyMag research internship
text: EnergyMag is a non-profit organization whose internship offers students an opportunity to delve into renewable energy research. Guided by mentors, you will study a specific company, technology, or market, gathering information through research and networking. The goal of your research will be to analyze the data and produce a report which will be published on the website. You can choose between a half-time internship that runs for 2-8 weeks or a quarter-time internship that runs for 1-9 months.
Updated text: Join EnergyMag, a non-profit organization, for an immersive research internship in renewable energy. Choose between a flexible half-time internship (2-8 weeks) or a quarter-time internship (1-9 months) to fit your schedule and interests.

title: ART 1101 Art as Experience
text: Art as Experience is an introductory course that expands a student’s understanding of the ideas and practices of art today. Studio projects will introduce a broad range of mediums from drawing and collage to digital photography and video installation. Students will explore and respond to resources at Cornell University and the course will be supplemented with readings, critiques and field trips. The course will culminate in an exhibition where students will be responsible for the organization and installation of self-directed art work.
Updated text: Embark on an artistic journey in ART 1101: Art as Experience! title: CS50's Introduction to Game Development
text:

Principles of 2D and 3D graphics, animation, sound, and collision detection

Unity and LÖVE 2D

Lua, C#

title: Bretton Woods International Economics Competition
text: In the Bretton Woods International Economics Competition, you will compete in groups of 2-4 to test your knowledge of microeconomics, macroeconomics, and general economic understanding. The competition involved 2 rounds - an online selection round consisting of an online quiz and a final in-person round where you must present solutions to economic policy problems.
demographics: Anyone currently enrolled in high school
location: The first round is online and the second round is in Bretton Woods, New Hampshire

title: Introduction to Probability Management
text: This course assumes that you are comfortable with Microsoft Excel, but you do not need training in statistics. This course will teach you how to recognise the flaw of averages , the arithmetic of uncertainty , and how to create interactive simulations .

title: HarvardX: Exercising Leadership: Foundational Principles
text:
